## Why a Python Extension Can Change the Runtime Mode

CPython 3.13 introduced experimental free threading, a configuration that can run with the global interpreter lock (GIL) disabled. Python extensions must explicitly declare support for this mode. If an extension is imported without that declaration, Python issues a warning and enables the GIL.

Declaring support for free threading is separate from making an extension’s code thread-safe. The declaration mechanism also differs depending on whether an extension uses multi-phase or single-phase initialization.

On Windows, extension builds do not automatically receive the `Py_GIL_DISABLED` compiler macro. The free-threading configuration can be checked through `sysconfig`.
